titulo: Should AI detectors decide if academic work is authentic?
temaCentral: Cada vez más universidades usan detectores de IA para revisar trabajos académicos. Debatir si un puntaje de detección puede servir como prueba para juzgar (y sancionar) a un estudiante, o si la evaluación debe cambiar.
preguntaGuia: Should a university sanction a student because an AI detector says their work was written by AI?
objetivoAprendizaje: Practicar el debate oral en inglés sosteniendo una postura con una razón concreta (un caso, un dato, una consecuencia) y respondiendo a lo que otras personas plantean.
instruccionesParaEstudiantes: Write in English and in your own words. Every argument needs a claim and a reason (a case, a fact, a consequence). Use 'because' or 'since' to connect them. Then listen to the others and connect your ideas: reinforce, counter, ask a question or concede a good point.

posturas.etiqueta: Detectors are valid evidence and sanctions are fair
Detectors are unreliable and must not be used as proof
Change the assessment: drafts, oral defense, process

ejemplosPorTema.bueno: AI detectors should not be used as proof because they can flag honest students, and a false accusation can damage a student's record without any real evidence.
ejemplosPorTema.porque: The weak one is an opinion with no reason; the strong one states a claim and explains the concrete harm it causes.

ejemplosPorTema.bueno: Sanctioning with detectors is fair because plagiarism software is already accepted as evidence, and a high detection score gives the university a first reason to ask for an explanation.
ejemplosPorTema.porque: The weak one is a generalization with no case; the strong one compares with an accepted practice and limits the claim to a first step.

ejemplosPorTema.malo: Teachers should just change the exams.
ejemplosPorTema.bueno: Universities should assess the process because drafts and short oral defenses show how a student thinks, and no detector is needed to see whether the ideas are really theirs.
ejemplosPorTema.porque: The weak one gives an order without a reason; the strong one names the method and explains why it works.

ejemplosPorTema.bueno: Detectors are risky for second-language writers because simple, regular sentences look 'predictable' to the tool, so a student writing carefully in English can be wrongly marked as AI.
ejemplosPorTema.porque: The weak one is a vague statement; the strong one explains the mechanism and the consequence for a specific group.

promptSistemaFase1: Evaluate only whether the argument is written in English and has a claim and an explicit reason (a case, a fact, an example, 'because', 'since'). Do not judge whether the position on AI detectors is right or wrong. Only suggest: the decision belongs to the people who moderate.
promptSistemaFase2: Suggest possible connections between arguments (reinforcement, counterargument, dilemma, question, concession). The decisions belong to the people who moderate.
